steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
In a medium bowl, combine the eggs, milk, mayonnaise and cornstarch. Stir in the cheese, imitation crabmeat and pepper. Pour into the pie shell.
Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 35 to 40 minutes or until a knife inserted in the center comes out clean. Let cool slightly and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple Crab Quiche
raw_recipe.description: I love quiche and imitation crab. This combines the best of both worlds. It is a simple and versatile recipe that whips up in a jiffy.
raw_recipe.name: Simple Crab Quiche

review.reviewBody: This is a MUST!! I took the advise of others and used sour cream instead of mayo, an extra egg, extra pepper for spice, and I carmalized onions to add. I made it for Thanksgiving brunch and it was gone before I could even get a slice! My restaurant-owner family friend raved about it!! USE REAL CRAB!

So this was my first quiche ever and I must say it was a WINNER! My husband loved it. I did make a few alterations based on some of the prior reviews and comments. I sauteed red onion and garlic, diced up fresh spinach, used 2 eggs plus 1 egg beater; 1/4c olive-oil mayo and 1/4c sour cream instead of all mayo; a mixture of cheeses - cheddar/jack/queso, parmesan/romano and sharp cheddar; and added a T of heavy cream to the milk measurement; for spices I added a bit of Old Bay seasoning along with a little bit more pepper. With these alterations it took about 55 minutes to bake instead of the requisite 40 mins. Yummy! I can't wait to make it with other meats such as turkey sausage or ham.

This is my base recipe. I follow it to the letter with these exceptions: I use Miracle Whip instead of mayonnaise, flour instead of cornstarch, REAL jumbo lump crab meat and I add large or medium cooked, peeled and de-veined shrimp. I also add a little fresh dill to the mix before baking. I serve it hot and often with a side of pan seared salmon and a mixed green salad. It is VERY rich so a little goes a VERY long way!

I DID use the sour cream instead of the mayo; however, next time, I'm going to use Duke's mayo just to see what it tastes like! I also added an extra egg. Instead of milk, I used half 'n' half. I probably used more than 1.5 cups of Swiss but that stuff is hard to measure! I also added a T of flour, green onions, 1/2 tsp of Old Bay, a sprinkling of onion powder, and a tsp of garlic powder. 
I then topped it all off with Himalayan salt and black pepper. There was enough to make two nine inch pies. It was GREAT!!

I will definitely make this again! Like other reviewers I used sour cream instead of mayo and half and half instead of milk. I also used four different cheeses (Swiss, Colby/Jack, Provologne and Mozzarella) because that's what I had left over and added a pinch of red pepper flakes. For the crust I grated some stale bread, mixed it with melted butter and pressed into dish. Then I sprinkled Parmasean and an Italian 5 cheese blend over the crust and baked it for 10 minutes till browned and melted. Then I added the egg mixture. Yummy! Even surprised myself how good it was!

I've made this several times since I first found the recipe. The first time I made it I followed the recipe exactly and it was good, but we both felt like it was missing something. After several tweaks, I've got it right where we want it. 

I follow the basic recipe and I add 3 finely chopped green onions, 1 tsp Old Bay Seasoning and 1/2 tsp Lawry's Lemon Pepper. After I pour it into the crust I put a small can of French fried onion rings on the top and bake as directed. Fantastic!

Really good, easy recipe. Decided to make it spur of the moment because I had a leftover pie crust on hand. Went to Walmart for the ingredients I didn’t have on hand. No shredded Swiss so I went with Monterey/Colby. Used half and half imitation and real crab, which cut the cost of crab immensely, and since I like eggs, added 2. This will go into my dinner rotation and for that I’ll probably add spinach. Made a small fruit salad of black plums, raspberries, blueberries, and strawberries. Delicious.
I substituted real crab meat and doubled the recipe. It was beyond amazing

This was such an easy recipe to make , I used mozz. instead because that was all I had. I also added cooked minced onions, used a 1/4 cup of sour cream and 1/4 cup mayo., and toped with sliced tomatoes . A great brunch meal, or to take to a potluck.

Great recipe, and easily modified. I've made it twice. The first time with real crab and I would have given it 4 stars. Last night I made it with spinach, mushrooms and bay shrimp. I sauteed them with garlic, curry powder, olive oil, and Tabasco. I also added some sharp Cheddar Cheese and the extra egg. Awesome!!! Restaurant quality and sooooo easy. Will definitely make it again.

I used lite mayo, added chopped green onions as well as chopped bell pepper & added an extra egg. I omitted almost all the cheese & used about half a cup of shredded mozzarella, just on top. It would have been just perfect if I had remembered to remove the paper liner from the pie shell. LOL Was able to salvage it by using a huge pancake spatula to remove the egg, peeled the paper back some, cooked the pie shell for a few minutes because the bottom was underdone & then inverting the quiche back into the shell & peeled off the paper. If this hadn't worked, I'd be listing this as one of my cooking tragedies but all's well that ends well. ;o) The only thing I will do different next time (aside from removing the paper liner, of course LOL) is to cut up the crab meat ...I thought it would break down some while cooking but it didn't & the chunks were a little big. Served it w/ a salad w/ vidalia onion vinaigrette & for dessert, grilled fruit (cooked inside in a grill pan) w/ simple syrup. Fabulous summertime meal...despite the stupidity of the cook!

It was good, I guess. It was all eaten. I replaced the crust with a topping of toasted cornflakes and shredded cheese. That was the only part I really liked, even though I was looking forward to this meal.

Like other commenters, I substituted sour cream for mayo and added a third egg. I had a six ounce can of lump crab in the pantry, which drains to 3 to 4 ounces, and then I thin-sliced about 4 ounces of mahi mahi as the filler. I also thin-sliced a stalk of celery, a small onion, and added Old Bay seasoning. It was really good. The crab overpowered the mahi.

I have made both the crabmeat quiche as well as the breakfast alternate. Both are great!!! Added sautéed mushrooms, onion and Roma tomatoes (all diced). Only problem is I made way to much ingredients for one crust. Used the extra ingredients to make loaded eggs. These too were a hit!
Delicious! Only thing that makes it better is real crab meat.
My only additions were crumbled bacon, and sautéed onions...
Made this as directed and it was awesome. Will make it again.
This is my third time making this quiche
It's so easy, tasty and relatively inexpensive to boot! I used havarti this time... delicious!
We love this one.
